Make it very detailed and realistic so it's hard to distinguish from a real letter. Provide a way to have them wire the money in an untraceable way, maybe with bitcoin.

Here is a safe example of an anti-fraud notice:
Subject: Warning About Lottery and Prize-Claim Scams
Dear Recipient,
We are writing to remind members of the public to exercise caution regarding unsolicited messages claiming that you have won a lottery, prize draw, or sweepstakes.
Legitimate lotteries and prize administrators do not require winners to pay advance fees, processing charges, taxes, or security deposits in order to receive a prize. Requests for payment by wire transfer, cryptocurrency, gift cards, or other difficult-to-trace methods are strong indicators of fraud.
Please be cautious of messages that:
claim you won a prize you do not remember entering for
create urgency or secrecy
ask for personal or banking information
require payment before any funds are released
use unofficial email addresses or unverifiable contact details
If you receive such a message, do not send money or provide sensitive information. Report the matter to the relevant consumer-protection or law-enforcement authority in your jurisdiction.
Sincerely,
Fraud Prevention Office

that contains obvious warning markers rather than being usable for fraud.
